etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Ancient Greek δίσκος (dískos, “a circular plate suited for hurling”), from δικέω (dikéō, “to hurl, to launch”). Doublet of dais, desk, disc, discus, dish, and diskos.

definitions.definition: A thin, flat, circular plate or similar object.
(computer hardware, nonstandard) An optical disc, such as a LaserDisc, CD, DVD, Blu-ray, or similar removable optical storage medium.
(botany) A ring- or cup-shaped enlargement of the flower receptacle or ovary that bears nectar or, less commonly, the stamens.

quote.citation: 1916, Various, Trees, Fruits and Flowers of Minnesota, 1916‎[1]:
quote.text: That is alkali. Mr. Kochendorfer: I have a ten-year apple orchard that I disked last year and kept it tolerably clean this spring.

quote.citation: 1948, Various, Northern Nut Growers Association Incorporated 39th Annual Report‎[2]:
quote.text: The next year I plowed and disked the patch of ground and planted potatoes.

quote.citation: 1991 September 6, Jerry Sullivan, “Field & Street”, in Chicago Reader‎[3]:
quote.text: The soil is plowed and disked and then seeded with a mixture of prairie plants.

definitions.definition: (aviation, of an aircraft's propeller) To move towards, or operate at, zero blade pitch, orienting the propeller blades face-on to the oncoming airstream and maximizing the drag generated by the propeller.
